title: Special Array II
summary: An array is special if each pair of adjacent elements has different parity.
statement: An array is special if each pair of adjacent elements has different parity. Given an integer array nums and a 2D query matrix, determine if the subarray defined by each query is special. Return an array of boolean values indicating whether each queried subarray is special.
constraints: nums is nonempty; every query is an inclusive pair [left,right] within the array.
A subarray is special when every adjacent pair in it has opposite parity.
Return one boolean per query in the given order.
hints: A query fails exactly when its interior contains at least one equal-parity adjacent edge.
Build a prefix count of bad edges and compare the count at the query endpoints.
Subtracting endpoint prefix counts counts precisely the bad edges whose right endpoint lies in (left,right].
editorial: Subtracting endpoint prefix counts counts precisely the bad edges whose right endpoint lies in (left,right].

tests.explanation: The final adjacent values 2 and 6 are both even, so the queried subarray is not special.
The first query contains adjacent odd values 3 and 1; the second alternates odd and even.
